inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 184.087M cover-page shares at 2026-10-15 (Q3 2026 10-Q) plus the 1.205M Q3 2026 dilutive-securities adjustment (187.838M diluted less 186.633M basic weighted) = 185.3M. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the ~$1.3B/yr buyback is a distribution of the same FCF the model values and is value-neutral here. The count is two weeks later than the 30 September cash balance, so roughly $50-60M of October repurchases are in the count but not yet out of cash (~$0.3/share, accepted).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: ShareBasedCompensation $54.8M plus PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation $24.3M, summed because PulteGroup publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA figure
inputs.debt_detail: Senior notes $1,783.5M + other notes payable $25.4M = $1,808.9M at 2026-09-30 (Q3 2026 10-Q notes-payable table). Financial Services warehouse/repo borrowings are excluded: they fund $433.9M of mortgage loans held for sale and both are operating items. The Metrics.csv TotalDebt column (31-74) is the XBRL LongTermDebt tag, which is not the notes balance; do not use it. Cash $1,369.9M is unrestricted only (restricted $38.1M excluded). February 2026 refinancing pushed the nearest senior maturity to 2031.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. 10y UST ~4.1% + homebuilder beta ~1.35 x 5.0% ERP = ~10.9% cost of equity; debt ~12% of capital at ~5.0% pre-tax / 3.8% after tax; WACC = 10.0%. Same WACC in every scenario; cyclicality is charged once, in the scenario flows and weights, not again in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases (~$150M liabilities): lease expense is already inside SG&A and therefore inside the EBITDA margin (treatment B); lease liabilities excluded from net debt. No lease_cost_pct_path needed.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interests immaterial; flows are attributable. No NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.working_capital_note: A homebuilder's capital is inventory ($14.1B of house and land inventory at 2026-09-30 against ~$15.5B FY2026 revenue, ~0.9x). Over FY2016-25 inventory absorbed ~70% of each revenue dollar added and cumulative reported FCF was 69% of cumulative net income during 9%/yr revenue growth. wc_capture_pct is therefore NEGATIVE (growth consumes cash, decline releases it): -55% base/bull, -40% bear. In FY2026 the release has NOT happened: inventory rose $1.15B in nine months while revenue fell 10%, 9M operating cash flow was $637M and management holds FY2026 OCF at ~$1.0B on ~$5.3B land spend. The Y1 capex_pct_path entry is therefore calibrated so Y1 unlevered owner FCF lands at ~$0.8-0.9B (OCF ~1,000 - PP&E ~105 - SBC and equity-award taxes ~99 - interest income ~40 + after-tax cash interest ~80), which takes 13.0% of revenue in the base (11.8-12.2% bear/bull) rather than the 8.0% of the October build, whose Y1 FCF of $1.39B overshot the same guide. Y2-Y3 keep the prior 4.5%/2.0% taper (management signalled a further FY2027 land-spend cut and walked option contracts), then PP&E only from Y4.
inputs.margin_calibration: ebitda_margin_path is UNLEVERED adjusted EBITDA before SBC: pretax income + D&A + interest amortized through cost of sales - interest income + SBC. FY2016 14.7%, FY2017 13.5%, FY2018 15.6%, FY2019 15.6%, FY2020 18.1%, FY2021 20.2%, FY2022 23.1%, FY2023 22.7%, FY2024 23.4%, FY2025 18.2%, H1-2026 16.0%, Q3 2026 17.2% (pretax 625.2 + D&A 26.7 + interest expensed 28.6 - interest income 8.2 + SBC 10.5 on revenue 3,973.8), 9M-2026 16.4%. Pre-COVID normal ~15%, 10-year average 18.5% inflated by the FY2021-24 supply-shock regime. Base mid-cycle held at 17.5%: credit for consolidation, Del Webb mix and scale, but not for 2021-24 margins. Adding back capitalized interest is what makes deducting net debt once correct.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF with mid-cycle normalisation (dcf-methods routing: cyclical operating company -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md); same model as the 2026-10-02 build. UPDATE 2026-11-19 on the Q3 2026 10-Q and the lowered guide. FY0 = FY2025; Y1 = FY2026, of which nine months are reported (revenue 11,365, -10% YoY; NI 1,295, -25%). Guidance now 27,000-27,500 closings (was 28,500-29,000), Q4 gross margin 24.0-24.5%, SG&A 10.3-10.5%, OCF ~$1.0B, land spend ~$5.3B; demand fell sharply from September as mortgage rates approached 7.5%. CHANGED: (1) anchors to 2026-09-30 / 2026-10-15; (2) Y1 growth to the new guide (-10.3% base, -9.5% bull, -11.5% bear) and Y1 SBC to 0.64% (9M SBC 44.7 + equity-award taxes 39.6 annualised ~$99M); bear Y1 margin 15.5 -> 16.0 because nine months at 16.4% are in hand; (3) Y1 land-ahead-of-revenue capex calibrated to the ~$1.0B OCF guide (see working_capital_note); (4) base Y2-Y4 trough deepened and delayed (FY2027 growth -3 -> -5, margin 15.8 -> 15.0; FY2028 growth 3 -> 2, margin 16.3 -> 15.8; FY2029 margin 16.8 -> 16.5) and bull recovery pushed a year (FY2027 growth 2 -> 0, margins 16.8/17.6 -> 16.2/17.2) because the base's 6-6.5% mortgage-rate premise failed; (5) weights 25/50/25 -> 30/50/20. DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: base Y1 margin 16.3% (9M 16.4% and the Q4 guide confirm it); mid-cycle margins 17.5/19.5/15.0 and Y5-Y10 growth in every scenario (one bad quarter of orders is cyclical, not structural, evidence; a sustained gross margin below 23% or impairments beyond the $42M 9M run-rate would move them down, a rate fall with incentives under 8% would move them up); the bear's FY2027-35 recession path (already a -12%/-6% revenue, 9% trough-margin case; Q3 does not make it worse, only likelier, which is what the weight carries); Y2-Y3 capex taper; SBC 0.46% from Y2 (a second year of ~$40M equity-award taxes would lift it to ~0.6%); D&A, 24% cash tax, WACC 10%, terminal growth 2.5%, 12x cap, wc_capture. Owner FCF (last_fcf) = reported FCF 1,748.5 - SBC incl. equity taxes 79.2 - interest income 44.4 = 1,624.9, FY2025. Interest income is stripped (and cash held at face in the bridge) because the forward build is unlevered via the capitalized-interest add-back. Buybacks: $1,031.6M in 9M-2026 and $1,331.6M trailing twelve months of actual financing outflow (buyback_cash), so the flat count is funded many times over. Terminal cap 12x owner FCF in all scenarios binds below Gordon at 10%/2.5%, so terminal-growth sensitivity is muted by design. Street basis differs from house by only ~0.5% of revenue of SBC, the band is narrow, and the price sits above both, so band_position is outside 0-100. Roughly one quarter of Y1 FCF is still ahead of the September balance sheet; the rest is already in it (~$2.5/share overlap, accepted as in the prior build).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: mid-cycle judgment: US housing starts roughly flat plus 2-3% ASP/mix inflation; the equity CAGR (14.6%) is retained peak-cycle earnings net of buybacks and is not a repeatable revenue growth rate for a cyclical already past its FY2024 earnings peak
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 14.6% diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR 9.4% and from EPS 3yr CAGR 0.4%; FY2025 EPS is already below FY2022. Owner-FCF CAGRs are meaningless on their endpoints: FY2022 was an inventory-build trough (owner FCF ~$490M on NI $2.6B) so the 3yr figure is 49%, while the 5yr figure is -0.5%. Neither is used for projection.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes - interest income, FY2020 ~1,668, FY2022 ~490, FY2025 1,625. Reported and owner FCF CAGRs are within 3pp of each other: SBC is ~0.5% of revenue and is not where the growth is being paid for. Cash conversion, not SBC, is the swing: cumulative FY2016-25 reported FCF was 69% of net income because inventory absorbed ~70% of revenue growth.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 at the lowered guide: nine months reported 11,365 + Q4 ~7,275 closings x ~$555k ASP + ~$0.13B financial services/land = ~$15.5B, -10.3%. FY2027 -5%: Q3 orders -6% units with the September-October pullback not yet in closings, absorption 1.9/community/month, incentives 10.4%; backlog (10,298 homes, +4% YoY) cushions H1 only. FY2028 +2% as community count (1,077, +7% YoY) converts once rates stop rising; FY2029-31 4-5% recovery and 2.5-3% nominal thereafter, unchanged.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 16.3% (9M actual 16.4%, Q4 guided gross margin 24.0-24.5% against better Q4 SG&A leverage). FY2027 trough 15.0%: the year starts at the Q4 exit gross margin with SG&A at 10.3-10.5% on a smaller base. FY2028 15.8%, FY2029 16.5%, then the prior path to a 17.5% mid-cycle by FY2031, held.
base.capex_rationale: Y1 13.0% = ~0.7% PP&E + ~$1.9B of land and house inventory investment ahead of revenue, calibrated to the ~$1.0B FY2026 operating cash flow guide (inventory +$1.15B in nine months on falling revenue). Y2 4.5%, Y3 2.0% unchanged, then PP&E only with wc_capture carrying revenue-driven land.

bull.growth_rationale: FY2026 at the top of the lowered guide (27,500 closings, -9.5%). Mortgage rates retreat from ~7.5% through 2027 so FY2027 is flat rather than +2%, and the community-count growth turns into closings growth from FY2028; revenue reaches ~$22.7B by FY2035.
bull.margin_rationale: FY2027 16.2% and FY2028 17.2% (a year later than the October path) as incentives fall from ~10.4% toward 6% of price; gross margin recovers toward 27-28% with SG&A ~8.5-9%; mid-cycle 19.5%, still 4pp below the FY2022-24 regime, which is not assumed to return.
bull.capex_rationale: Y1 12.2% calibrated to the ~$1.0B FY2026 OCF guide; taper unchanged.

bear.growth_rationale: FY2026 at or below the low end of the lowered guide (-11.5%); then the unchanged recession path: FY2027 -12%, FY2028 -6%; revenue troughs at ~$12.7B (-27% from FY2025, far milder than 2006-09 given undersupply and balance sheets) and recovers slowly to ~$15.5B by FY2035.
bear.margin_rationale: FY2026 16.0% (nine months at 16.4% are reported; Q4 at ~15%). Thereafter unchanged: gross margin compresses to ~19-20% on price cuts and incentives, SG&A delevers to 12%, land impairments hit FY2027-28; unlevered EBITDA margin troughs at 9% and recovers only to 15% (the pre-COVID normal).
bear.wc_rationale: Inventory liquidation does generate cash in a downturn (PHM OCF was +$1.2B in 2008), but turnover slows and spec inventory builds, so the release per revenue dollar lost is set at 40% rather than 55%.
bear.capex_rationale: Y1 11.8% calibrated to the ~$1.0B FY2026 OCF guide; Y2 2.0% then PP&E only, unchanged (land spend is cut hard in a recession).

scenario_narratives.base: The cycle has turned harder than the October build assumed but does not break. Mortgage rates near 7.5% since September cut FY2026 closings to the lowered 27,000-27,500 guide (revenue ~$15.5B, -10%) and carry the weakness into FY2027: revenue falls another 5% as Q3-Q4 orders (-6% and worse) reach closings, incentives stay above 10% of price, gross margin sits near the 24.0-24.5% Q4 exit rate and SG&A near 10.3-10.5%, for a 15.0% unlevered trough margin. Rates ease only gradually; from FY2028 the community count (1,077, +7%) and structural undersupply lift closings and the margin recovers to a 17.5% mid-cycle by FY2031, below the 10-year average because FY2021-24 was a supply-shock regime but above the ~15% pre-COVID norm on consolidation and Del Webb mix. FY2026 cash flow is held to the ~$1.0B operating cash flow guide because inventory is still building (+$1.15B in nine months); land spend tapers through FY2028 and cash conversion then normalises to ~85% of NOPAT at 3% growth. Terminal value is capped at 12x owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: The September rate spike proves a shock, not a regime: mortgage rates fall back toward 6% during 2027 and below it in 2028. FY2026 lands at the top of the lowered guide, FY2027 is flat, and incentives fall from 10.4% toward 6% of price so gross margin recovers toward 27-28% with SG&A back near 8.5-9%. Del Webb (orders +11% in Q3 2026 even as the total fell 6%) and Florida (+6%) show the less rate-sensitive half of the mix holding, the build-to-order shift protects margin through the transition, and scale lets the top builders take share from private builders squeezed on land and labor. Mid-cycle margin settles at 19.5%, still 4pp below FY2022-24; revenue reaches ~$22.7B by FY2035.
scenario_narratives.bear: The demand pullback that began in September 2026 becomes a 2027 recession with rising unemployment hitting an already affordability-strained buyer. FY2026 misses the low end of the lowered guide, closings fall 12% in FY2027 and 6% in FY2028; price cuts and incentives push gross margin to 19-20%, SG&A delevers to 12% on a smaller base, and owned land bought at FY2023-25 cost assumptions is impaired (Texas and West segment pretax income were already down 63% and 57% in Q3 2026). The unlevered margin troughs at 9% in FY2028 and recovers only to the ~15% pre-COVID norm, with revenue still below FY2025 in FY2035. Inventory liquidation releases cash through the trough (as it did for PHM in 2008-09), which is what keeps this bear from being a solvency event: the nearest senior maturity is now 2031, the revolver runs to 2031, and the balance sheet carries $14B of inventory at cost.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 30% (25% in October, 15% house default): the trigger the prior build named for the bear path, mortgage rates above 7%, has occurred; management cut closings guidance for the first time this year, traffic is -14%, and it called its own outlook 'not a very upbeat message'. Bull 20% (was 25%): it now needs rates to fall some 150bp from ~7.5% and incentives to taper, two independent things, from a worse starting point. Base 50%: the base itself was lowered to absorb the guide cut and a deeper FY2027 trough, and the balance sheet (12% debt-to-capital, $1.4B cash, no senior maturity before 2031) lets management run the defensive plan it described.

valuation_philosophy.summary: PulteGroup is valued as a cyclical operating company on owner FCF with explicit mid-cycle normalisation rather than by extrapolating FY2024 peak earnings. The flows are unlevered (capitalized interest added back, interest income stripped) so the $439M of net debt is deducted exactly once; SBC is expensed and the count held flat; land investment is charged through a negative working-capital capture on revenue growth plus a front-loaded land-ahead-of-revenue capex line, which is what reconciles the model to PulteGroup's actual 69% ten-year cash conversion. Risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and the 30/50/20 weights, with a single 10% USD WACC and a 12x terminal cap appropriate to a sector that has never sustained a premium multiple.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin judgment: each 1pp of terminal unlevered margin is worth roughly $8-9/share; the 17.5% base sits between the ~15% pre-COVID norm and the 18.5% ten-year average and could be wrong in either direction

Land cash conversion: FY2026 is calibrated to the ~$1.0B operating cash flow guide, but the Y2-Y3 taper (4.5%, 2.0% of revenue) assumes management follows through on cutting land spend; each extra $1B of inventory build is ~$5/share
Mortgage-rate path: rates reached ~7.5% in September 2026 and the base now assumes only gradual easing; a further rise or a 2027 recession is the bear path, a retreat toward 6% the bull path
Terminal cap: 12x owner FCF is a judgment; the Gordon value at 10%/2.5% is 13.7x and the stock's own history supports 8-12x earnings

Impairments in the bear case reduce book inventory rather than cash and are not separately modelled; the bear relies on inventory liquidation generating cash, which assumes homes still clear at lower prices
Financial Services warehouse borrowings are treated as operating and excluded from debt; a secondary-market disruption would change that
